title: Ragdoll death — physics-driven launch from blast direction + per-limb spring flail (supersedes the S100 canned death tween)
intent: Replace the canned root-Transform death tween from S100 KABOOM-SLAPSTICK-DEATH (launch-up + Y-spin) with a physics-driven ragdoll: impulse direction comes from the blast that killed the bomber, root.position follows a gravity arc with horizontal travel away from the blast, all 9 limb pivots are released into spring-damped flail driven by the root's angular + linear velocity. Zero gameplay impact — RoundResolveSystem still sees alive=false on the same frame as today; auto-restart timing unchanged. Pure presentation layer that makes death READABLE as 'this blast killed you' instead of the current direction-agnostic 'you launched upward and disappeared'. Reuses the spring infrastructure from GDP-2026-05-22-004 — ragdoll is its generalisation across all 9 pivots during the 0.6 s death window.
rationale: Sources: `docs/game-design/characters-and-visual.md` §3.3 (DeathAnimationSystem already noted 'optionally scatter limb nodes with spring physics for the ragdoll feel'), `docs/game-design/visual-style.md` §6.2 (death-plume + slapstick tone), `docs/game-design/gameplay-systems.md` §6.1 (the round resolution depends on the alive-flip frame, NOT on the death animation completing). User request 2026-05-22: 'может нам ещё ragdoll сделать для персонажей чтоб их слегка откидывало взрывом'. The S100 slapstick tween was the right MVP-1 stopgap (death needed to feel like SOMETHING). Now that the multi-mesh tree (S102) + spring system foundation (GDP-2026-05-22-004) + accessories (GDP-2026-05-22-003) are in flight, the proper version costs little and delivers the modern-bomb-em-up feel (Boomerang Fu / Bombergrounds: Reborn vocabulary).
acceptanceHints: Depends on GDP-2026-05-22-002 (migration — death animation runs in kaboom-crew side, NOT bench) AND GDP-2026-05-22-004 (spring-sway — ragdoll reuses its k=18 / damping=0.4 constants for limb flail).

SUPERSEDES: the canned launch-up + Y-spin tween from S100 KABOOM-SLAPSTICK-DEATH (in examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/death-animation-system.ts, plus the GDP-2026-05-20-004 extension that added the Y-axis hop). That tween is removed/replaced in this story — not layered on top. The S100 tween's user-visible effect (bomber visibly exits the arena over ~0.5 s) is preserved with the new physics-driven path delivering a richer version.

Trigger: BlastEvent overlaps a bomber's cell + BomberStats.alive flips false (same frame as today). The death-animation-system captures the blast direction from the BlastEvent payload at the moment of the alive-flip and stores it in a new component on the dying bomber:
RagdollState { blastOriginGx, blastOriginGz, deathStartedAt, magnitude }

Direction vector: target - origin in world XZ space (normalised). magnitude = 1.0 for a single blast; clamp(1.0 + 0.4 * (additionalBlasts), max 1.8) for chain reactions hitting the same bomber in the same frame.
PHASE A — Root arc (replaces the S100 vertical-hop tween):
Initial velocity vector: (direction.x × magnitude × 1.6, +2.4, direction.z × magnitude × 1.6) in cell-units-per-second.
Per fixedUpdate: vy += gravity (-9.0 cell/sec², a tuned arcade gravity, NOT real Rapier — pure scalar math). Update root.position by velocity × dt.
Horizontal travel: with the above constants, the bomber lands ~0.7 cells from the death cell after 0.6 s. Vertical peak ~0.85 cells above ground. Matches the user's 'слегка откидывало' brief.
Angular velocity: cross(direction, worldUp) × magnitude × π — produces natural tumble (a blast from the east tips the bomber over toward the west). Apply as root.rotation deltas per tick.
PHASE B — Limb spring flail (NEW):

At alive-flip frame, the 9 limb pivots (LimbPivots component) each get a small angular impulse derived from the root's INSTANTANEOUS velocity at that frame: pivot.rotation gets a random-but-deterministic offset of ±15..40 degrees, then the spring-sway system from GDP-2026-05-22-004 takes over.
'Random-but-deterministic': derive the per-pivot offset from a hash of (bomber entity id, blast origin cell, pivot name). Same inputs → same offset. NOT Math.random.

Spring constants: REUSE the soft-attached defaults (k=18, damping=0.4). No new parameters. The spring-sway system already runs over any tagged entity; ragdoll adds a transient tag (RagdollLimb) to each pivot during the death window.

Spring-sway system needs ONE small extension: it must look at the parent ROOT's angular velocity, not the immediate parent's, when computing the spring target. Otherwise nested pivots (e.g. elbow inside shoulder) double-compensate and stiffen. Acceptable change since soft-attached accessories are also parented to root-relative ancestors.
PHASE C — Despawn:

After 0.6 s (configurable via component field — currently hard-coded), the bomber entity + its full 10-mesh + 9-pivot tree is despawned. Same as the S100 behaviour. Auto-restart timing (3 s post-RoundState.phase flip) is independent of the death-animation duration.
GAMEPLAY INVARIANTS — all preserved:
RoundResolveSystem still sees alive=false the same frame as today. The death-animation duration does NOT delay round resolution.
The bomber's GridOccupancy entry clears the same frame as alive-flip (existing rule). Other bombers + blasts pass through the corpse during the animation.

Hit-recoil from GDP-2026-05-22-004 still fires on the same frame as the lethal blast — on the bomber's TORSO entity, before the ragdoll takes over the ROOT. Hit-recoil is on a child Transform; ragdoll is on the root Transform; they don't fight.
DETERMINISM:
Spring integration uses fixedUpdate dt only (no wall-clock).
All randomness derives from (entity id + blast origin + pivot name) — no Math.random.

The bot-vs-bot regression test must continue to resolve within budget with bit-identical round outcomes. Visual ragdoll trajectories may differ from a hypothetical pre-merge replay; gameplay state must not.
MULTIPLE-BLAST EDGE CASES:
Multiple blasts on the same bomber in the same frame: impulse summed (vector-summed), magnitude clamped at 1.8 as noted above.
Bomber killed by its own bomb: blast origin = bomber's current cell → direction is zero-length → fall back to (0, +1, 0) launch with no horizontal travel + zero tumble. Same as S100 visual.

Bomber killed while standing on a kicked bomb that detonated mid-slide: use the bomb's last grid cell at detonation time as the origin. Bomb cells move at most one cell per kick, so this is well-defined.
PERFORMANCE:
Per dying bomber: 1 root physics integration + 9 spring integrations per fixedUpdate × 0.6 s × 60 Hz = ~360 spring updates total per death. Trivial.
At most 4 simultaneous dying bombers in standard arena → 4 × 9 = 36 active spring entities at peak. Within the 4 ms / frame anim budget from visual-style.md §11.
NETWORK (forward-looking, not in scope for this story):

Server-authoritative mode (GDP-2026-05-20-007 multiplayer): server fires the alive-flip + sends the blast origin in the snapshot. Client computes the ragdoll trajectory LOCALLY. Two clients watching the same death may see slightly different ragdoll paths (different floating-point drift) — that is acceptable because gameplay state is server-authoritative and visuals are local.
BENCH PREVIEW:

Bench-animation-system gains a 'ragdoll' dropdown option. Selecting it triggers a synthetic RagdollState write on the bench bomber with a UI-driven blast origin (small +X / +Z offset arrows in the bench panel). Useful for tuning the constants visually.
After the ragdoll completes, the bench resets the bomber to upright + alive — the bench has no round-restart concept.
UNIT TESTS:
Direction → impulse vector mapping (e.g. blast from east → west-ward launch).
Magnitude clamp at 1.8 with simultaneous blasts.
Self-bomb edge case → pure vertical launch.
Determinism: same blast origin + same bomber entity id → bit-identical pivot offsets.
Total duration check: ragdoll completes within 0.6 s ± dt; despawn fires at the end.

Gameplay invariant: alive-flip frame, GridOccupancy clear frame, RoundResolveSystem trigger frame are all the SAME frame as before. Ragdoll only changes the body's visual trajectory, not the rule clock.
VISUAL QA (manual):
4 bombers spawned via bench. Trigger ragdoll on each from a different blast direction. Verify:
- bomber visibly tumbles AWAY from the blast
- limbs flail visibly during the launch (no stiff plank)
- peak height ~0.85 cells; horizontal landing ~0.7 cells from start; total ~0.6 s
- chain reactions (multiple synthetic blasts) produce a more dramatic launch but stay readable (no flying off the arena)
ANTI-PATTERNS (explicit, do not ship even if tempting):
- NO Rapier rigid-body simulation. Procedural spring math only. Per visual-style.md §11 perf budget + per the 'grid-authoritative, not physics-authoritative' rule (gameplay-systems.md §3.1).
- NO blood / debris particles. Visual-style.md aesthetic (industrial diorama, slapstick tone). Death-plume + ragdoll body is sufficient.
- NO trupp lying on ground for seconds. Despawn at 0.6 s, same as today.
- NO camera shake driven by ragdoll. Camera shake is reserved for 'your own bomb killed you' (gameplay-systems.md §6).

- NO ragdoll on non-lethal hits. Even when Shield power-up lands (future story), surviving a blast triggers hit-recoil (GDP-022-004) only, not full ragdoll. Reserving ragdoll for death keeps the visual semantically loaded.
OUT OF SCOPE (explicit):
Real rigid-body physics. Cartoon-far-launch. Trupp persistence past 0.6 s. Per-limb collisions with arena geometry. Customisable ragdoll constants per recipe (cosmetic-unlock territory).
